evidence.summary: At regular intervals Voyager crew vanish as apparently confused Nyrians appear in their place.
Early Nyrian arrivals claim ignorance and describe themselves as accidental victims of the same phenomenon.
Torres determines the exchanges are produced by technology rather than the proposed natural wormhole or flow-field explanations.
Nyrian infiltrators use the exchange sequence and prior computer knowledge to seize Voyager after most crew have been removed.
Taleen says the Nyrians capture ships, stations and colonies by gradual replacement and confine displaced populations in tailored habitats instead of conventional warfare.
Voyager crew discover many artificial environments aboard a biosphere vessel holding populations from numerous prior captures.
Janeway and Tuvok identify the translocator as the exchange mechanism with a range exceeding ten light-years and the ability to route between habitats and Voyager.
Paris and Torres exploit a frigid habitat the heat-sensitive Nyrians cannot tolerate while Janeway gains translocator control.
Janeway threatens to move Nyrian leaders into the hostile cold habitat unless Voyager and all prisoners are released.
Dammar surrenders; Voyager is returned, the other captive populations contact their homeworlds, and the translocator is disabled before departure.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A seemingly random exchange of strangers is revealed as a methodical Nyrian ship-seizure system supported by a long-range prison/translocator network.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Natural-anomaly hypotheses and confused-victim presentation are preserved as earlier states later overturned by technical and behavioral evidence.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Nyrian provision of comfortable habitats is real but does not negate that the populations are held without consent.
